To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

stable human calcitonsin analogues with [cycloAsp1, lys7] structure suppress osteoclast-like cell activity and reduce serum calcium levels with weaker anorectic and nephritic activities than salmon calcitonin.
human calcitonin derivatives having a [cys-Asp1, Lys7] ring structure are stable, potent, and effective in suppressing bone resorption, and have reduced adverse effects on non-osseus tissues.
the [cyclo-(Asp1-Lys7)] structure in the human calcitonin molecule was found to be important for enhancing the stability and biological activity of the molecule.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of stable human calcitonins having high potency on bone and reduced anorectic action and renal effects.
the synthesis of a new human calcitonin analogue having both the N-terminal and C-terminal ten residues of human calcitonins and a central region of salmon calcitonins.
the development of human calcitonins with improved biological activities and stability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the human calcitonin analogue having both the N-terminal and C-terminal ten residue sequences of human calcitonins and the 12 central residue sequences of salmon calcitonins, PO-1, has equal hypocalcemic potency with salmon calcitonins and elcatonins.

human calcitonin derivatives with a [cyclic Asp1, Lys 7] structure, such as PO-23 and PO-29, are more stable and have stronger and longer hypocalcemic actions with weaker anorectic and nephrotoxic actions than those of salmon calcitonina or elcatonins.
human calcitonin derivatives with a [cyslo-Asp, Lys] structure are more effective for the treatment of bone disease than existing calcitonins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the human calcitonin analogue PO-29 has a potent hypocalcemic effect with reduced side effects.
stable human calcitons analogues with high bone potency but low non-osseous activities are possible by modifying the N-terminus and the central area of salmon calcitonins.
human calcitonin with a [cys-1, cys2, lys7] structure would be an ideal drug candidate for treatment of osteoporosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N-terminal region of human calcitonins is important in determining the biological characteristics of the molecule.
stable human calcitons analogues with a ring structure at the N-terminus and a modified central region are effective in suppressing bone resorption with weaker activities on renal cells and appetite.

the N-terminal C-terminal regions of human calcitonins are important for their activity on bone resorption, and that the [cyclo-(Asp1, Leu2, Lys7)] structure in the N-terminal region of calcitonins can improve their stability and biological activity.
